- K613 · 2026-09-30 · the Action layer's notifications and filings (Bob, in BOB #74's session, answering K611's three points) · (1) Choosing an action includes setting its notification schedule, defaults preselected; a deadline notice's response offers another reminder or no further reminder (DEC-10, recorded in `NOTIFICATIONS.md` at D-125: remind again at a further increment, or stop; DEC-69: never nag). So the overdue/deadline reminder is not repeated unless the member asks, and the class question of K611 (1) is answered by the member-set schedule, not by re-notification. (2) A litigation-hold reminder, like every notification, is not repeated unless the member asks; the hold may be cleared when responding to it, and if not cleared it stays open until cleared: that is its disposing door. (3) Filing templates: every filing has case-specific parts; a group builds a library of boilerplate templates over time; where none fits, members use the assistant to draft one for the action at hand (a proposal a member adopts, D2), and a derivative of it may be kept as a template for later use. No job invents legal text. The drafts' citation of DEC-70 for notifications is a mis-citation (DEC-70 is basis-leg severance); ACTION_DESIGN #1 corrects it and folds these three answers into its drafts. · P5, P17.
- K614 · 2026-09-30 · the Action layer's reminders (replaces K613 (1)'s citations; evidence: DEC-94, Bob 2026-09-29, in `docs/development/DECISIONS.md` on `claude/gallant-brown-zg0wc1`, PR #4, not yet on `main`) · The governing ruling is DEC-94: (1) a deadline reminder is the member's own request, set up when the action is chosen in the action plan, perhaps by a default the member sees and can change at that moment (nothing preselected unseen, DEC-77); a further reminder is one the member accepts, perhaps at the system's suggestion; it fires as asked; (2) as a deadline nears, the item's position, colour or wording may change: display, not a notification; (3) no outside channel (email, push); (4) overdue is new and re-notifies once (DEC-10); "due within N days" is not new unless the member asked for it. K613 (2) (the litigation hold stays open until cleared, cleared when responding) and (3) (the template library) stand. - K1755 · 2026-10-06 · policy, Bob's (K1547 corrected) · Evidence (P15): Bob, 2026-10-06, on K1547's record: "Only the subscription token was limited to the member; I didn't limit API keys." His words of 2026-10-05 were: "Yes, the system will support API keys. But we'll also support a per-member subscription token that will only be used by that member. And finally, we'll support a version of the UX that doesn't use AI." K1547 recorded them as "their own API key or their own Claude subscription token, each held for and used only by that member", carrying K1502's "no group-wide … Claude account" over to API keys; K1502's own answer ("Own subscriptions only") and its evidence (the Consumer Terms; Claude Code's rule on Free, Pro and Max credentials) concern subscriptions only. So the record went beyond Bob's words. **Ruled, replacing K1547's reading and K1502's API-key clause (the rest of K1502 stands):** three options. (1) **An API key at the group level:** an administrator may hold one Anthropic API key for the group's copy; it serves the group's members. (2) **A subscription token at the member level:** held for and used only by that member (K1502, K1537 and K1547 stand for it). (3) **No AI:** a group may run without the assistant, and a member reached by no account uses the product without AI, whose capabilities are a subset of those with it. A member's own API key (built in T33) stays: Bob's words do not exclude it. **BOB's details (P17), Bob may change any:** the group key is set, switched on or off (off by default) and removed only by an active administrator, sealed at rest and never shown, exported or logged; a member's own account, when held, serves that member's acts first, and the group key serves members without one while it is on; the copy's ceiling (K1450) caps the group key's use, and each member's day counts against it; each member is told, before their first ask under the group key, that their questions and the material read go to Anthropic under the group's API account (D311's disclosure, K1478 (i)). In T34, now (P19: credentials' T34 job has not started; its users are in L6 and L11): credentials R26 retired, the group key's Rs added; agent-model, ai-runs, agent-worker resolve the account per act; instance-setup offers the choice at setup (group key, members' own accounts, or no AI); op-declarations, admission, control-plane route the administrator's acts; canon (Assistant and AI Roles, Capability Ladders) amended; NOTICE to UX-DESIGN. · P15, P17, P19; replaces K1547's reading.

- K1880 · 2026-10-06 · doctrine, Bob's (N680 Q1; P17) · Bob: "The assistant is a helper, but also a powerful research planning engine. So it may use search tools (like Bing, etc) to find the information. The search engine may return references to a website that the research tool may scan looking for the documents of interest. All of this should be allowed. But when it comes to actually harvesting for the record, the researcher delegates the capture to the civicsmith substrate to retrieve it in a way that provides a high grade." So: the assistant's discovery (web search, reading result pages, scanning a site for documents) is open to any public site; nothing it reads that way enters the record; whatever enters the record is fetched by the substrate's capture (capture-requests, acquisition), never by the assistant, so the record's grade is the substrate's. Folded into the security review (F2's answer: the guard is on what reaches the record and on what leaves inside an address, not on where the assistant reads) and the investigation engine (K1627). - K2352 · 2026-10-08 · N812 A1–A4, Bob's (P17) · Asked on the page https://claude.ai/artifact/EDBXX6r47QPQKx4XD5yQTf (K2349), Bob: "1. B 2. A 3. B 4. The limits an account owner sets is the limit for their account. (If a project has an account, then that's the one used with project-level limits.) If not but a member has an account, then that's used with those limits. If neither, then the group account with its limits. Every account owner can set usage limits." Ruled: (1) B: a member may lend their own subscription to a project as the project's account (this revises K1547/K1755's member-only subscription for that case). (2) A: any one owner of a project sets its AI settings alone, each change recorded with who and when and visible to every owner. (3)–(4) An account owner's limits are the limits of their own account only. For a member's act: if the project has an account, that account is used, with the project's limits; if not and the member has an account, the member's, with the member's limits; if neither, the group's, with the group's limits. Every account owner can set usage limits. BOB's details (P17): the administrator's copy-wide ceiling becomes the group account's own limit (per member as the group sets it), binding no other account; an account at its limit refuses and the act does not move to the next account (Bob's "that's the one used"); the draft's "a member may always name their own account" is dropped (not in his words). Open with Bob, raised at once: AT-3 (Consumer Terms) forbids making a Free, Pro or Max account "available to anyone else", and AT-16 forbids routing requests through such credentials on others' behalf, so (1) as ruled conflicts with Anthropic's terms for those plans; Team and Enterprise are unaddressed (U-1). Until he answers, no lending is built. · P17; K1547, K1755, K1502, K2349.

Measured: a repo-less cloud session (haiku) went from creation to its first reply in about 6 s (PROBE remote link #1, `session_01HNTyUhzsasyyL7g8GaX23b`, archived; usage 47,724 cache-read, 14,885 cache-write, 2 input, 4 output); `claude -p … --cloud` from this container failed "Session expired" (it holds no claude.ai login). Composite route to test: a session made once per run (routine fire or the sessions service), then driven turn by turn with `claude -p --cloud <id>`, context kept; it needs a member's claude.ai login with the sessions scope (the docs cap it at 30 days). - K3678 · 2026-10-17 · A job that scans stops and its reading is pruned, Bob's (P20, P13, P17; K3586, K3588) · Ruled (Bob, 2026-10-17, in BOB #202's session): "I believe that any job that only scans its record should immediately stop and prune the record so that it can be fully read. If there is still sufficient context, then that job can continue fully read in. If the session's context is too full at that point, then a refreshed session should be spawned. This replacement session should then be able to read its record fully." BOB's details (P17), BOB's reading of "its record" as each document the job must read (its reading set, mechanics §6 step 2), its own record among them: a job about to read a document only in part stops at once and posts `BLOCKED` (cause `reading`, naming the document and its size); a document the job owns (its record, its module's files) it prunes itself, keeping every binding word; a build-state document (not the job's to write) BOB trims or splits (mechanics §17) the same turn and answers with a `CHANGE`; the job then reads it whole and continues if its context is under half its window, else posts `BLOCKED` (cause `context`) and BOB restarts it (§5.4), the new session reading it whole. A job that has already completed on a part-read document re-reads it whole and confirms or corrects its work before it is merged (PROGRESSIONS #13, K3679). `roles/JOB.md` and mechanics §6 change to say so only once Bob approves their exact text (K1258); until then this ruling governs and each START states it. · Bob

- K4182 · 2026-10-20 · The scanner has no signatures: ClamAV refuses its mirror; fixed by ClamAV's own updater, never by borrowing its identity, BOB's (P7, P17; K3658, K3656) · Diagnosis worker (sonnet, medium; `build/plan/walk-T51-live/scanner-diag.md`): `clamav/state.json` reads `last_error: REFUSED:main.cvd:403` since the first run; `clamav/` holds no signature set; every `/scan` answers `not_scanned` at once (no container reached), so the 27 files stay due; the plane's scan wake (every ~5 min), the cron, the containers are all healthy. The cause: database.clamav.net refuses file-scanner's own downloader (its User-Agent `file-scanner/<v> (signature mirror; as cvdupdate)`); it answered a request bearing cvdupdate's or ClamAV's own User-Agent. **Ruled:** sending another tool's User-Agent is working around the site's own bot protection, which K3658 forbids; the fix fetches the signatures with ClamAV's official updater under its own identity, by one of: (a) the FileScanner container running ClamAV's `freshclam` (already in its image) and keeping the set where the scanner reads it, or (b) a scheduled run of ClamAV's `cvdupdate` filling the `clamav/` mirror; the job chooses by ClamAV's published mirroring guidance and rate limits, read live. Also (file-safety): the Security screen names files tried and refused "waiting", hiding the reason; it states that the scanner has no signatures and since when. Both are fix-round entries (FR-SCAN), with tests at each module's interface (a mirror refused shows on Security; a set fetched by the official path is loaded). · K3658

- K4385 · 2026-10-21 · Why BOBs reach for a force-push, and the fix, BOB's (P13, P15, P16; §5.3 (1), §16; K3969, K3977, K4384; Bob, 2026-10-21: "Figure out why you're doing forced pushes in the first place and fix that.") · **Cause:** §5.3 (1) says only "push `job/T<n>/<module>` from the tranche branch", and no tool does it, so every BOB hand-writes the git command. Job branches are reused round after round (`job/T51/<module>` already exists, behind the tranche), and "set this branch to that commit" is written by habit as a forced push (`git push -f origin tranche:job/...`); the rule against it lived only as a lesson in rulings-active §4 (K3969), read once at takeover and not at the moment of writing the command. Auto mode refused it each time (K3977, K4384), which is the guard working, not the cause removed. **Fix:** the act is now a tool, `mail jobbranch --module <m>` (civicos-process `prep/jobbranch-K4385` @ 1d8f9e2; tests 157/157, its own test proving a diverged branch is refused and left untouched): it creates the branch at the tranche tip or fast-forwards it there by a plain push, and refuses a branch holding commits the tranche lacks, naming the remedy (the job merges the tranche in; a finished job is merged into the tranche first); it contains no force path. rulings-active §4 now says a job branch is moved only by it and no session hand-writes a push to one. BOB #242 uses it from the prep worktree until T51's close carries it to the process repository's `main` (M-T51-6 now names it). Mechanics §5.3 (1)'s wording is left as it is (the rule it states is unchanged; only the means is a tool). · K4384

- K4566 · 2026-10-22 · The watchdog: efficient and bulletproof, Bob's (P17; K4563, K4565) · **Bob (2026-10-22), in BOB #251's session:** "The Worker alarm is a watchdog timer. The mechanism it uses should be efficient - but mission-critical bulletproof". **Ruled:** the Worker's scheduled trigger is a watchdog timer over the object's alarm; it is efficient and mission-critical bulletproof. **BOB's details (P17), binding on round 6's plane and scheduler entries:** (1) it only checks and re-arms (one small call to the object a cycle: is an alarm set and in the future, did the queue run within two cycles; if not, set it to now), never runs owed work, reads no document, and finishes in milliseconds; (2) it shares no failure with what it watches: a different platform mechanism (the Worker's cron, not the object's alarm), no dependency on the ledger's rows or any heavy read, idempotent so a repeated or late fire is harmless; (3) it never fails silently: every path is bounded in time and caught, a failed call is retried on the next cycle, and each fire records its own last-seen instant beside the scheduler's heartbeat, so the process's checks see a dead watchdog as well as a dead alarm; (4) it is proven at the platform's real behaviours before the deploy: a spent alarm, an alarm killed more than seven times, a restart at deploy, the object busy with a long read, a fire that arrives twice or late; and checked live after each deploy by the smoke; (5) cost: one cron fire every few minutes per team, the shortest interval the plan justifies against K4565's "without human awareness" and the cost of a call. · K4565

- K4993 · 2026-10-24 · Tests kept current with the code they stand in for, Bob's direction, BOB's details (P7, P11, P17; K4990, K4989, K1258) · **Bob** (2026-10-24, in BOB #283's session): "When the tests of a module haven't been updated to reflect the evolving code (both that module's code or the code of an adjacent module that the test simulates), its tests may pass even though they're no longer really testing anything or no longer provide complete code coverage. An end-to-end test like the control plane, a simulated walk, or a live walk of a deployment may find a problem caused by this incorrect test fixtures. Finding these failures later in the build/test of a round/tranche is much more expensive to fix than it would have been had the tests been kept up to date to reflect changing code and requirements." **BOB's details (P17):** the root is a copy: a hand-written stand-in is the neighbour's answer frozen on the day it was written, so P11's rule (a job changing a provided service runs its users' tests) catches nothing, the users' tests passing against their own stale copy. So, extending K4990: (1) a provider's published fixture is produced by its real code when the test runs, never stored, so a provider change reaches every user's test in the provider's own job, where P11 already runs them; (2) a new check, `fixtures`, beside `words`, refuses a test that hand-builds another module's answer or stub (the patterns of plan §7 item 7 (a)'s audit), so none can return; its mechanics text goes to Bob rendered for approval before it binds (K1258), proven on the next fix round first; (3) a test that no longer tests anything is found by breaking the code it names: at each round end a worker breaks, one at a time, the lines a sample of each changed module's requirement tests cover and confirms a test turns red (a mutation sample); a mutant no test notices is a test gap of that round, its module's job. Plan F9 §7 item 7 (e)-(g) in the same commit. · K4992
